Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GreenWave Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a landline, or click the raise hand icon if using the webcast. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GreenWave Energy Corp's results for the third quarter. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Sustainability Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Operating Officer; Nina Keller, Chief Strategy Officer; and David Leung, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. GreenWave Energy Corp continues to demonstrate its leadership in the renewable energy sector, achieving a record-breaking performance in the third quarter. Our success is a testament to our unwavering commitment to innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence.

Today, I want to highlight eight key aspects of our performance: our impressive growth in operating capacity and generation output; the new power purchase agreements we've secured along with favorable pricing; the continued expansion in our gross and operating margins; our successful tax equity and project-level financings; the significant additions to our development pipeline and key milestones achieved; the strong progress on construction and upcoming commercial operation dates; our capital recycling through asset sales; and our strategic priorities and outlook for the coming periods.

Now, I'll hand the call over to Michael Chen to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Our financial performance in the third quarter was exceptional. Revenue reached $1.2 billion, representing a 28% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 28.2%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $190 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $150 million, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $2.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are significantly raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Good afternoon, everyone. As your CFO, I'll now dive into our core operational metrics: operating capacity in megawatts and actual generation output in gigawatt-hours. These are the lifeblood of our clean energy portfolio, reflecting not just our scale but our ability to deliver reliable, dispatchable renewables amid volatile weather patterns and grid constraints.

Starting with the headline numbers: As of September 30, 2024, our total operating capacity stood at 8,450 MW, a robust 18% year-over-year increase from 7,150 MW at the end of Q3 2023. This growth was driven by 1,050 MW of new assets reaching commercial operation date during the quarter, including the full 650 MW Desert Bloom solar-plus-storage hybrid project in California's CAISO market and 400 MW from two onshore wind repowerings in ERCOT. On the generation side, we produced 14.2 GWh across the first nine months of the year, up 14% from 12.5 GWh in the same period last year. This translated to a blended portfolio capacity factor of 24.8%, slightly ahead of our internal guidance despite below-average wind speeds in the US Plains and Europe—our year-to-date average wind capacity factor hit 32.1%, while solar came in at 23.4%, buoyed by high irradiance in the Southwest US.

By technology: Onshore wind, 58% of our portfolio at 4,900 MW operating, generated 9.8 GWh YTD, up 16% YoY. Key driver was the repowering of our 250 MW Legacy Plains Wind Farm in Texas, where we swapped out 80 aging 2 MW Vestas V80 turbines for 102 state-of-the-art GE Vernova 4.5-138 platforms. This boosted site-specific capacity factors from 28% to 38% post-repower, thanks to taller hubs and larger rotors capturing stronger upper-atmosphere winds. We're on track to repower another 600 MW across PJM and MISO by mid-2025, targeting a 10-15% uplift in annual output per MW.

Utility-scale solar PV, 28% of portfolio at 2,350 MW operating, output reached 3.9 GWh YTD, a 22% YoY jump fueled by the COD of Desert Bloom, featuring 1.2 million bifacial TOPCon modules from LONGi at a DC/AC ratio of 1.4:1. This project's 22.8% capacity factor exceeded expectations due to rear-side albedo gains from our agrivoltaic sheep-grazing setup, which also unlocked USDA grants under the Inflation Reduction Act. We've also begun early deployments of heterojunction tech in our 300 MW pipeline, promising 2-3% higher efficiencies versus PERC in dusty Southwestern conditions.

Offshore wind and emerging tech, 9% of portfolio at 750 MW operating: Our 400 MW stake in the UK’s Hornsea 3 project—developed with Ørsted—ramped to full output in Q2, contributing 1.1 GWh at a stellar 42% capacity factor, aided by Siemens Gamesa SG 14-222 DD turbines. Additionally, our 350 MW/1,400 MWh BESS portfolio in ERCOT and ISO-NE dispatched 0.4 GWh of ancillary services revenue, with round-trip efficiencies averaging 92% on our latest Fluence Cube systems. Hybrids now represent 25% of new CODs, aligning with FERC Order 2023 incentives for co-located firming.

Battery energy storage systems, 5% of capacity at 450 MW/1,100 MWh: Not a primary generator but critical for output optimization—our systems arbitraged $45/MWh spreads during summer peaks, enhancing wind/solar effective capacity by 15-20% via time-shifting.

Regionally: United States, 65% of capacity at 5,500 MW: Dominant growth engine at 22% YoY capacity expansion, with ERCOT delivering outsized returns amid record data center load growth from hyperscalers like Google and Microsoft. However, we navigated 2.5% curtailment in Texas due to queue backlogs—our 2 GW interconnection queue positions us well post-FERC reforms. CAISO benefited from LCFS credits on Desert Bloom, while PJM's 18-month RTEP approval cycle accelerated three 200 MW solar PPAs.

Europe, 25% of capacity at 2,100 MW: Flat YoY at 5.9 GWh output, pressured by Germany's negative pricing episodes but insulated by 300 MW repowering in the Netherlands under REPowerEU yielding €120/MWh fixed PPAs. Offshore exposure hedges continental wind variability.

Asia-Pacific and LatAm, 10% of capacity at 850 MW: Early innings with 150 MW COD in Australia's NEM using Trina Vertex modules and a 200 MW wind farm in Chile's Atacama grid. Output here grew 35% YoY, tapping copper mine PPAs at $60/MWh—all-in IRRs above 12%.

We've seen a clear shift toward hybrid assets, now 40% of our 15 GW development pipeline, as grids demand firm renewables—think wind+solar+BESS colocation slashing LCOE by 20% to $35-45/MWh. Supply chain tailwinds persist, with US module costs down 25% YTD under IRA domestic content bonuses—we hit 55% DC for federal tax credits. Weather headwinds shaved 1.2% off Q3 output versus plan, but our AI-driven forecasting partnered with Clir Renewables improved short-term accuracy to 92%, optimizing curtailment avoidance.

Challenges include interconnection delays—average 3.5 years in PJM/MISO—and blade supply for offshore, but our $2.5B liquidity and 4.2x net debt/EBITDA position us to opportunistically acquire stalled projects.

For FY2024, we now guide to 18.5-19.0 GWh total output and 8,900 MW year-end capacity, with 1.2 GW CODs skewed to Q4. FY2025 brings 2.5 GW additions, targeting 25%+ portfolio growth and capacity factors expanding to 26% via repowers and 800 MW new BESS. This supports our reiterated $1.2-1.3B adjusted EBITDA guidance, with 70% of output locked in investment-grade PPAs averaging 8-year terms at $50/MWh blended.

Good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to dive into one of our key performance drivers: our Power Purchase Agreement—or PPA—pipeline and pricing dynamics. PPAs remain the bedrock of our revenue visibility, providing long-term, investment-grade offtake for our utility-scale solar, onshore wind, and hybrid projects. In Q3, we made significant strides, underscoring our disciplined origination strategy amid a competitive landscape shaped by the Inflation Reduction Act's PTC and ITC extensions, as well as Europe's REPowerEU push.

Headline: we secured 1.2 GW of new PPAs across five projects, bringing our total contracted backlog to 8.7 GW as of quarter-end—a 25% increase year-over-year. This includes our largest-ever single-asset deal: a 450 MWdc solar-plus-storage PPA with a leading hyperscaler for our Desert Bloom project in California's CAISO market. This 15-year agreement, priced at an all-in $32 per MWh including a 200 MW / 800 MWh BESS component, features a 2.5% annual escalator tied to CPI and prioritizes dispatchable power during peak net-load hours. The hybrid configuration leverages our proprietary SolWind Optimizer software for AI-driven battery dispatch, achieving modeled capacity factors above 35%—a 15% uplift over standalone PV thanks to our use of N-type TOPCon bifacial modules with 23.5% efficiency.

Complementing this, we locked in 350 MW of onshore wind PPAs in ERCOT with two investment-grade utilities at an average of $38/MWh over 12 years. These build on our Black Hawk Wind Farm expansion, incorporating GE Vernova's 5.0 MW turbines with 60-meter hubs. We also announced a 250 MW offshore wind PPA in the UK's North Sea with Ørsted as co-developer, at £48/MWh indexed to UK CPI, reflecting the premium for fixed-bottom foundations and our integration of Siemens Gamesa's SG 14-222 DD turbines targeting 55% capacity factors.

North America accounted for 65% of new bookings, driven by data center demand—we've now signed PPAs with three Fortune 50 tech firms representing 1.1 GW in the past 12 months. Europe contributed 25%, bolstered by the EU's Net-Zero Industry Act, while our first 100 MW entry into Australia's NEM with AGL Energy rounds out the mix at AUD 55/MWh.

Our fleet-wide blended average PPA pricing stands at $36 per MWh for new contracts, down 4% quarter-over-quarter but flat year-over-year when adjusted for escalators. This reflects industry trends—PPA prices compressed 12% since 2022 due to module price deflation to $0.22/W and turbine oversupply. Solar PPAs averaged $31/MWh pre-ITC, wind at $41/MWh, hybrids at $37/MWh thanks to storage arbitraging negative pricing.

Our all-in PPA pricing—net of $28/MWh average LCOE—delivers unlevered IRRs of 9-11%, above our 8% hurdle. Compared to merchant markets like CAISO's $15/MWh negatives, our PPAs provide stability. We've embedded shapeable products in 40% of new deals, boosting effective yields by 5-7%.

These wins validate our Hub-and-Spoke origination: co-locating near load centers to capture locational premiums. We're advancing perovskite-silicon tandems and airborne wind energy to extend PPA tenors. Our 15 GW pipeline has 40% pre-PPA'd, positioning us for $4-5 billion in annual backlog additions.

I'll now turn to our margin performance, where we continue to demonstrate strong execution. As a leader in utility-scale solar PV modules, bifacial trackers, and integrated BESS, with over 15 GW deployed globally, our margins reflect vertical integration—from polysilicon to EPC—and focus on high-efficiency N-type TOPCon modules, now 65% of shipments.

Gross margins delivered 28.2%, up 320 basis points YoY from 25.0% and 110 bps sequentially. This marks our highest in two years, on track for 30%+ by 2026.

Drivers: Favorable product mix—BESS deployments surged 45% YoY to 1.2 GWh, with margins over 35% via LFP packs and Aurora software. This offset softer module ASPs at $0.28/W, but premium TOPCon commanded 15% pricing edge.

Supply chain efficiencies: $45 million cost savings QoQ from Vietnam fab at 95% utilization, CTM yields at 98.5%. Polysilicon at $8.5/kg, module COGS down 12% to $0.20/W.

U.S. gross margins at 31% boosted by IRA 45X credits adding $0.07/W on 85% domestic content. Europe steady at 26%, APAC at 24%.

Operating margins achieved 12.4%, up 280 bps YoY. OpEx at 15.8% of revenue. R&D at 4.2% focused on HJT modules and GreenH2 pilots. SG&A leveraged to 8.1% via AI sales automation.

These trends underscore our Margin First playbook: vertical integration covering 70% of stack; tech roadmap with perovskites projecting $0.15/W COGS; PPAs and VPPs locking 85% capacity factors; hedging 80% polysilicon.

We guide Q4 gross margins to 28.5-29.5% and full-year operating margins to 12-13%.

Before we move on, thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to provide a detailed update on our capital structure, focusing on tax equity financing and project-level financing. These enable scaling our 5.2 GW operating portfolio and 12 GW pipeline. In Q3, we achieved financial close on over $1.8 billion in new financings, YTD total $4.2 billion—up 28% YoY.

Tax equity remains primary for monetizing IRA attributes. Investors like JPMorgan, Bank of America provide capital for ITC at 30% plus adders, PTC at $27/MWh, and MACRS depreciation.

In Q3, two facilities totaling $850 million. $450 million partnership flip for 450 MW Desert Sunlight Expansion solar-plus-storage, with LONGi bifacials and Tesla Megapack—tax equity IRR 7.8%. $400 million lease-pass-through for 300 MW Plainswind II wind in ERCOT. Post-flip, we retain 85% cash flows.

Tax equity funded 65% of Q3 capex, yields compressing to 7.2%. U.S. Southwest outperforming.

Project-level financing: non-recourse debt atop tax equity, 60-70% debt. Q3: $950 million across four assets. $320 million green loan for 250 MW Horizon BESS at SOFR +185 bps. $450 million for 400 MW Aurora Solar.

Debt margins widened 25-40 bps, but 85% hedged to 4.1%. Back-leverage boosted IRRs.

Diversifying to Brookfield, AIP. U.S. 70%, ramping APAC. FY24: $6-7 billion financings. Leverage at 3.5x.

I'll now turn the call over to Lisa Patel to discuss our project development activities.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Our project development pipeline continues to grow rapidly, with 28.4 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring a substantial number of new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth.

Thank you, Michael. Now, turning to one of our strongest differentiators: our development pipeline additions and project milestones. A robust pipeline is the lifeblood of long-term value creation, especially amid IRA tailwinds, falling module prices, and corporate PPA demand. In Q3, we added a record 3.2 GWdc, bringing total to 28.4 GWdc—up 45% YoY, top tier with NextEra and Orsted.

Solar: 2.1 GWdc added, 62% of pipeline, including 1.2 GWdc bifacial TOPCon with trackers targeting LCOE <$25/MWh. Standout: 450 MWdc Horizon Valley Solar in CAISO with agrivoltaics.

Wind: 850 MW, 450 MW onshore ERCOT with Vestas V162-6.2 MW >45% CF; 400 MW offshore U.S. Northeast.

BESS: 250 MW/1 GWh, 150 MW hybrid PJM, 100 MW Australia NEM.

U.S. 68% or 2.2 GW; Europe 480 MW; APAC 540 MW.

Milestones de-risked 1.8 GW: NTP on 500 MW Texas wind; FID for 300 MWdc SolSmart Solar; Interconnection for 400 MW BESS ERCOT; permitting for offshore NY Bight and India agrivoltaic.

Hybrids 35% of pipeline, 20-30% higher IRRs. AI yield optimizer +8% P50. Q4: 2.5-3.0 GW adds, 1.2 GW milestones. $4.2B expected revenue to 2030 at 18% IRR.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing groundbreaking technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. We believe that these technologies will revolutionize the energy landscape.

Next, Tom Hargrove will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. Sustainability is deeply ingrained in our corporate culture, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that advance sustainability.

Now, Raj Singh will provide operational highlights.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Tom. Our operational performance remains exceptional. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets. We are implementing best-in-class practices in areas such as asset management, maintenance, and supply chain management. We are also investing heavily in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to excel.

Nina Keller, can you provide an update on our strategic initiatives?

Nina Keller:
Thank you, Raj. We are focused on executing our long-term strategic plan, which includes expanding our presence in key markets, diversifying our product offerings, and strengthening our partnerships. We are also actively exploring new opportunities in emerging areas such as green hydrogen and carbon capture.

Thank you, Michael, and good afternoon, everyone. I'll now turn to our construction pipeline, a cornerstone of our growth. We have 12.5 GW backlog across solar, wind, and BESS. YTD first power at 1.2 GW, 15% ahead, positioning for 4.8 GW COD by 2025 YE, supporting $1.2-1.4B FY25 EBITDA.

Americas: Texas Solar (1.8 GWdc), Rio Grande 650 MWdc at 78% complete—95% foundations, 85% First Solar Series 7 panels at 21.5% efficiency, trackers 92%. COD Q2 2025, PPA $38/MWh. 300 MW/600 MWh BESS at 45%.

California (800 MW hybrid): Mojave SunWind 500 MWdc solar +300 MW wind at 62%—wind TGs 75%, solar 55%. COD Q4 2024 solar, Q1 2025 full. 400 MWh Fluence.

EMEA: North Sea Offshore 750 MW at 35%, COD H2 2026. Spanish PV 400 MW at 88%, Trina Vertex N.

APAC: Australia 1.1 GW at 70%, COD Q3 2025. India 500 MW at 52%, COD Q4 2025.

Modular construction compressed timelines 18%. 72% of 2025 CODs on/ahead schedule.

And finally, David Leung, can you address our risk management strategies?

David Leung:
Thank you, Nina. We have implemented robust risk management strategies to mitigate potential risks associated with our operations, including market risks, regulatory risks, and environmental risks. We are continuously monitoring and evaluating our risk profile and taking proactive steps to manage these risks effectively.

Thank you, Michael, and good morning, everyone. I'd like to dive into our capital recycling and asset sale transactions, a cornerstone of our playbook. Capital recycling involves selling stabilized assets post-COD, recycling proceeds into greenfield pipeline without leverage or dilution—delivering 14% compounded IRR vs. 6.5% WACC.

Q3: two sales totaling 1.2 GW, $1.85B gross. 750 MW Southwest Solar Portfolio to Brookfield/pension at 7.8% yield—14.2x multiple, 15.2% IRR. 450 MW wind to Clearway at 8.2% yield, 42% CF.

$1.4B net liquidity. FY: $3.2B proceeds.

Trends: yields 7-8.5%, IRA premiums. U.S. 75%, Europe 300 MW YTD, APAC first floating solar.

Optimization: divested $12B since 2020 into 15 GW pipeline—next-gen solar, offshore, H2. FY25: $4-5B recycling.

I'll turn it back to Sarah for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you all. In conclusion, GreenWave Energy Corp had a truly exceptional third quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our unwavering focus on sustainability will continue to drive long-term growth and success.

Thank you, Operator, and good afternoon, everyone. As we wrap up a strong Q3 with 28% YoY revenue growth driven by 3.2 GW deployments, I'm excited to outline our strategic priorities and outlook for Q4 2024 and FY2025. Our Clean Tech portfolio—bifacial PERC solar, flow batteries, green H2 electrolyzers—positions us amid LCOE <$25/MWh and hyperscaler demand.

Q4 priorities: 1.8 GW deployments, 800 MW Gemini hybrid COD. North America 65%, IRA $450M PTCs. Perovskite pilots to 25%+ efficiency. Q4 revenue $1.35-1.45B, EBITDA 24-26%.

FY2025: $6.0-6.4B revenue, 28% growth, 12 GW deployments. Pillars: H2 to $600M; U.S. 55%, Europe 25%; margins 28-30%; SBTi 50% reductions.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
What are your plans for investing in new technologies such as green hydrogen?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for the question, John. Green hydrogen is a key pillar of our innovation roadmap, and we're ramping investments significantly. In FY2025, we're targeting 500 MW of electrolyzer deployments, partnering with leaders like Plug Power on PEM tech to produce green H2 at under $2/kg. This builds on our 700 MW pre-FID queue in the Permian, stacked with 45Q CCUS credits, delivering 20%+ IRRs through long-term offtake with industrial hyperscalers. We've allocated $250 million from Q4 capex to pilots, including flow battery integration for grid stability, positioning us to capture 10% of the U.S. market by 2028 amid IRA Section 45V incentives.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy market?

Sarah Thompson:
Great question, Emily. Competition is intensifying, but our vertical integration—70% of the stack—and tech edge like perovskite tandems keep us ahead. We're outpacing peers with 28% margins vs. industry 22%, leveraging IRA domestic content for premiums and Hub-and-Spoke origination near data centers for 10-15% locational upside. Recycling $3.2B YTD funds selective acquisitions of stalled assets, while our 28.4 GW pipeline conversion at 65% ensures scale. Discipline on 8% IRR hurdles and 80% hedged commodities mitigates price wars.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Can you discuss the potential impact of climate change on your operations?

David Leung:
Thanks, Mike. Climate change poses both risks and opportunities, which our robust framework addresses. Extreme weather shaved 1.2% off Q3 output, but AI forecasting with Clir Renewables hits 92% accuracy for curtailment avoidance. We're hedging resource variability via hybrids (40% pipeline) and geographic diversification—65% U.S., 25% Europe. Resilience investments like taller hubs boosting CF 10% and BESS for 15-20% effective capacity uplift are key. SBTi-validated Scope 1/2 cuts to 50% by 2025, plus insurance covering 105% EPC overruns, keep impacts minimal at <2% EBITDA risk.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Laura Kim:
What are your expectations for the long-term profitability of your renewable energy projects?

Michael Chen:
Laura, long-term profitability remains strong, with unlevered IRRs of 9-11% across new PPAs net of $28/MWh LCOE. Post-flip tax equity retains 85% cash flows, back-leverage lifts to 11.5%, and hybrids add 20-30% via stacking. FY25 EBITDA $1.6-1.8B at 27% margins, ROIC 15-18%, supported by $36/MWh blended pricing, 70% locked IG PPAs, and recycling yielding 14% compounded. Even with LCOE at $25/MWh per Lazard, our tech roadmap—HJT, perovskites—projects sub-$20/MWh by 2027.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, there appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for any closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of GreenWave Energy Corp. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
